The MACD vendor reported close_10_ema at **2355.12** vs. snapshot **2354.93**. All figures below use the **verified snapshot** values.

---

## 2. Market Structure: What 2026 Actually Did

The raw OHLCV tells a clear four-act story, all anchored to dated prices:

1. **January distribution → collapse.** Peak close **3354.72 (2026-01-14)**, then a waterfall to close **2445.09 (01-31)** and **1821.68 (02-05)**, with the intra-period capitulation low of **1748.63 (02-06)**.
2. **A second, deeper bottom in June.** Close **1568.77 (06-06)** on the lowest print of the year — this is the base, and the 200 SMA has been grinding *up* since, which is why the long-term trend is still technically constructive.
3. **The August breakout.** Close jumped from **1916.46 (08-18)** to **2251.46 (08-19)** — **+17.5% in one session** — on volume of **29.6B vs. 6.8B** the prior day. That is a genuine volume-confirmed regime change, followed by **2515.28 (08-21)**. Momentum extended to **2776.47 (09-21)** with an intraday high of **2805.50**.
4. **October distribution (the current regime).** The break happened in two sessions: **2697.52 (10-06) → 2573.53 (10-07) → 2471.91 (10-08)**, i.e. **−8.4% over two days** on ~20.1B volume each day. Since then every rally has failed at a *lower high*: 2534.70 (10-11) → 2496.63 (10-13) → 2470.77 (10-21) → 2357.62 (10-28). Today's **2262.34** closed the sequence.

**Net:** ETH-USD is **−18.5% from the 09-21 closing high** and **−32.6% from the 01-14 peak**, but still **+44% above the 06-06 closing low** and **+4.8% above the rising 200 SMA**. This is a **medium-term downtrend nested inside an intact long-term uptrend** — the single most important framing for the trade decision.

---

## 3. Indicator-by-Indicator Reading

**Trend / Moving Averages.** The stack is cleanly bearish in sequence: 2262.34 (price) < 2354.93 (10 EMA) < 2406.51 (20 SMA / Boll middle) < 2529.95 (50 SMA) — with only the 200 SMA at **2159.18** left below price. The **50 SMA has turned down** (2551.01 on 10-21 → 2529.95 today) while the **200 SMA is still rising** (2153.28 → 2159.18). The 50/200 gap is ~371 points, so no death cross is imminent; the practical bear signal today is simply that rallies into the 10 EMA / 20 SMA are being sold. The 10 EMA is now **sloping down and only ~92 points above price**, meaning short-cover rallies will be shallow.

**Momentum (MACD family).** The MACD line went **negative on 10-11 (−2.07)** and has bled to **−62.38**, ~9 points below the signal line. Critically, the **histogram improved from −36.68 (10-10) to −5.99 (10-28)** — a textbook "less-bearish" repair that a momentum trader would have read as a base forming — and then **re-widened to −9.29 today**. That is a *failed* momentum recovery, which is materially more bearish than a steadily negative histogram, because it shows the dip-buying impulse that carried 10-26 → 10-28 (2320.28 → 2357.62) was exhausted in three sessions.

**RSI.** **31.63**, the lowest print since the June low zone and below all of October's prior readings (range 33.7–45.4). Price made a lower close vs. 10-26 (2262.34 vs. 2320.28) and RSI made a lower low (31.63 vs. 33.71), so there is **no bullish divergence yet** — the downside is still impulse-driven, not exhaustion-driven. The 10-24→10-28 RSI recovery (36.37 → 39.14) also failed. RSI in the low-30s in crypto is typically *the middle* of a leg rather than the end of one, so this is a "get closer to a real stop/entry level" signal, not a buy signal.

**Volatility (Bollinger + ATR).** The **close (2262.34) is below the Bollinger lower band (2271.46)** — a band break — and today's true range (118.99 pts) exceeded the ATR (86.97), confirming the move is expanding rather than compressing. Note the *shape* of the bands: the middle band has fallen from 2683.93 (10-07) to 2406.51, and the lower band has been **flattening** (2281.38 → 2271.46 over the last 7 sessions) while price falls toward it. That combination — descending midline, flattening lower band, price exiting below it — is characteristic of a **trend leg rather than a mean-reversion bounce setup**. ATR at ~3.8% of price means a naive 5% stop is inside the noise; position sizing must be built off ATR, not round numbers.

**Volume.** Today's 13.06B is **~1.12× the prior 20-session average (~11.7B)** and ~38% above yesterday's 9.45B — i.e. **elevated but not climactic**. Compare with the 10-07/10-08 breakdown sessions (~20.1B each, ~1.7× average). The absence of capitulation volume is a warning: forced selling has not obviously been completed, and the volume pattern so far reads as distribution continuation rather than exhaustion.

---

## 4. Synthesis: Three Scenarios with Explicit Triggers

| Scenario | Trigger (concrete levels) | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| **Bear continuation (base case)** | Close **below 2252.86** (today's low) and RSI < 30 with widening histogram | Trend leg extends; next magnet is the **200 SMA at 2159.18** (≈1.2 ATR below today's close), then the Aug-19 breakout shelf at **2251.46 → 1906–1966 zone** |
| **Relief bounce** | Reclaim of **2271.46** (boll_lb) then **2354.93** (10 EMA) on >14B volume | Mean-reversion into the **2406.51** mid-band; a *tradeable* bounce but a **lower high** unless 2529.95 is taken |
| **Trend repair** | Daily close **above 2406.51** (20 SMA) and MACD histogram crossing back positive | First evidence the 10-08 breakdown is being filled; only then does 2529.95 / 2541.56 become the battleground |
| **Regime break (long thesis dead)** | Sustained close **below 2159.18** (200 SMA) | Long-term uptrend breached; opens the June–Feb structure (1852–1966, then 1568.77) |

**Bias:** The evidence supports **selling/rallying into resistance rather than bottom-fishing**. Five of six trend/momentum gauges are bearish (price < 10 EMA/20 SMA/50 SMA, MACD negative & below signal, histogram re-widening, RSI making lower lows, close outside the lower band). The two things arguing *against* a fresh short at this exact price are (a) RSI at 31.6 with price outside the lower band — statistically stretched for a 1–2 day horizon, and (b) the **rising 200 SMA only ~4.6% / ~1.2 ATR away**, which is the highest-probability zone for a responsive bid. That asymmetry says: **new shorts belong on bounces into 2355–2407, not on the current bar; and any long taken here is a scalp with a very tight, very explicit invalidation.**

---

## 5. Actionable Insights for the Trading Desk

1. **Do not chase the band break.** Shorting at 2262 with RSI 31.6 and price 1 band-width below the mean has a poor location-to-invalidations ratio; the nearest structural stop (above 2371.85, today's high) is ~4.8% away while the next magnet (2159.18) is ~4.5% away — roughly 1:1 reward at entry.
2. **Preferred short entry:** fade a reclaim of **2340–2360 (10 EMA)** or a failure at **2400–2407 (20 SMA / Boll mid)**; stop above **2425**; targets 2271 → 2190 → 2160. This puts the trade *with* the dominant structure (lower highs + negative MACD + downtrending 10 EMA).
3. **Preferred long entry (counter-trend, reduced size):** only on a **defensive hold of the 200 SMA at 2159**, defined as a session that breaks below and closes back above it (or a daily close in 2145–2175 with RSI < 28 and *bullish* histogram divergence). Stop **below the 2100–2075 shelf**; target the 10 EMA / 20 SMA at 2355–2407. This is a mean-reversion trade, **not** a trend trade, and must be sized as such.
4. **Risk sizing:** use ATR-14 = **86.97**. Set stops at **1.5×ATR ≈ 130 points** from entry for swings, and halve notional relative to an August-volatility position — current ATR/price (~3.8%) is roughly **double** the mid-August regime (~45–65 ATR). A fixed-dollar stop from September is now guaranteed to be noise-triggered.
5. **Structural stop-loss discipline:** the 50 SMA at **2529.95** is the "trend is wrong" line for any October short; the **2159.18** 200 SMA is the "regime is wrong" line for the whole post-June long thesis. Mark both.
6. **What would change my mind:** a close above **2406.51** with a positive MACD histogram and volume > 20B — that is the first time since 10-08 the lower-high sequence would be broken. Until that print exists, treat rallies as distribution.
7. **Watch the divergence you don't yet have:** with RSI at 31.6 and no bullish price/RSI divergence, the "bottom" signal is *absent*, not merely early. Do not pre-position for it.

---

## 6. Caveats

- Only ~10 months of 2026 data is in scope; the "June low" and "January peak" are period extremes, not necessarily all-time ones.
- Bollinger/moving-average values are recomputed daily and move; support/resistance levels cited are *prior observed price prints with dates*, and no bounce at any level has been validated by a subsequent tool output.

# ETH-USD Sentiment Report — 2026-10-22 to 2026-10-29

## Source-by-source breakdown

### 1. News headlines — Yahoo Finance
**Status: unavailable.** Yahoo Finance returned `DATA_UNAVAILABLE` for ETH-USD, with no news articles tagged to the instrument. This is a data gap, not a negative event for ETH-USD. Because institutional framing is normally the slow-moving anchor for sentiment, the absence of news reduces the robustness of the overall read.

### 2. StockTwits — retail-trader sentiment
The StockTwits block is small and time-clustered: 16 of 30 fetched posts were screened as ETH-USD-related, and all visible posts are from 2026-10-29 between roughly 20:09 and 20:53 UTC. This makes it a snapshot of acute retail reaction rather than a balanced sample across the full week.

**Classifier stance:** 2 bullish, 5 bearish, 4 neutral, 5 unclear.  
**User-labeled sentiment:** 2 bullish, 7 bearish, 7 unlabeled.  
**Bearish/bullish ratio among user-labeled posts:** 7:2, or 78% bearish of the labeled subset.  
**Bearish/bullish ratio under the Jev classifier:** 5:2, still net bearish.

The bearish examples are strongly capitulatory in tone:
- `@Eretheum`: “dead as fuck. 60k on deck” — extreme bearish framing.
- `@I_am_Sparta`: “complete destroying” and “this goes to Zero...” — capitulation/panic tone.
- `@DannyTanner1`: “complete destroying”, “Only reacts to downside in tech while ignoring every single rally up. Worthless trash.” — frustration with ETH-USD’s failure to track upside in broader risk markets.
- `@hookerm`: “bye bye” — short/capitulation framing.
- `@Cvn71`: “I guess it goes back down onto 2000. I’ll just lower my average.” — bearish expectation mixed with averaging down.

The bullish examples are sparse and less articulated:
- `@flopy`: bare bullish label.
- `@BullMine`: “bottom signal,” tagged bullish.

The unlabeled posts contain both bearish and counter-bearish evidence:
- Bearish or fragile structure: “last bulls hope is inverse h&s on weekly”; “1900”; sellers realizing losses.
- Potentially bullish supply/demand signals: `@9owls` claims “225,000 ETH have been bought off of exchanges today,” describing the largest one-day net buying spree they have seen; this is a meaningful off-exchange accumulation signal, though it is a single retail post and should be treated cautiously.
- `@CPA_` says “binance hack…. Should stabilize…,” implying an event-driven disruption but with a stabilization thesis.

**StockTwits signal:** Retail sentiment for ETH-USD is clearly bearish in tone, with capitulation and downside targets in the $1,900–$2,000 range. A small contrarian bottom-fishing pocket exists, but it is not dominant.

### 3. Reddit — community discussion
Reddit provides only light ETH-USD discussion: 5 of 10 fetched posts were screened as ETH-USD-related. Classifier stance: 0 bullish, 1 bearish, 4 neutral, 0 unclear. There are no vote or comment counts, so engagement cannot be inferred.

The subreddit mix matters:
- **r/ethereum** had only one recent ETH-related post, and it was not a market-thesis post: a user accidentally sent ETH from Binance to Robinhood via BSC and asks whether it is lost. This is neutral for price sentiment but negative for user-experience perception around self-custody, bridging, and exchange support.
- **r/CryptoCurrency** had two posts: one speculative AI/crypto payments discussion and one data post about top blockchains by USDC circulating supply. Neither is explicitly bullish or bearish for ETH-USD, but both are more macro/ecosystem-neutral than price-negative.
- **r/CryptoMarkets** contained the most relevant trading evidence:
  - A post about shorting ETH on Kraken at 20x leverage, where fees erased profits. This is not a fundamental ETH-USD thesis, but it shows a retail trader attempted bearish exposure and was frustrated by execution costs.
  - A post on Arthur Hayes/Maelstrom selling a roughly $22.3M crypto book, including ETH, ENA, UNI, ETHFI, AERO, PENDLE and ZAMA, with Bitcoin noted below its 50-day average. This is a notable de-risking event and aligns with the X chatter about Hayes’s ETH sale.

**Reddit signal:** ETH-USD discussion is muted and mostly neutral. The community did not generate bullish conviction posts. The one clear bearish/trading-action item is indirect: a shorting fee complaint plus an institutional/whale de-risking story. Reddit is therefore less emotionally bearish than StockTwits but does not offset the negative tone elsewhere.

### 4. X — real-time trader, analyst, and news-account chatter
X is the most informative source in this dataset. The retrieved sample contains high-impact bearish evidence from large accounts and on-chain trackers, plus meaningful but lower-magnitude contrarian bullish positioning.

**Dominant bearish evidence:**
- `@WatcherGuru`, one of the highest-engagement posts in the sample, reported crypto dumping, ETH below $2,350, BTC below $80,000, and more than $200M in leveraged long liquidations in 60 minutes.
- `@coinbureau` reported ETH slipping under $2,300 after the Fed held rates, with more than $100M in long liquidations in two hours, citing persistent inflation, rising oil prices, and geopolitical tensions.
- `@coinbureau` also noted ETH fell below $2,300 for the first time in two months, with ETH down 3.7% versus Bitcoin’s 2% drop, and cited U.S. spot Ether ETF net outflows of $485M from Oct 14–22 per Farside.
- `@lookonchain` ETF-flow updates show ETH ETF outflows across multiple days:
  - Oct 27: -38,303 ETH / -$89.07M one-day; -81,754 ETH / -$190.12M seven-day.
  - Oct 28: -27,418 ETH / -$64.04M one-day; -96,485 ETH / -$225.35M seven-day.
  - Oct 29: -9,081 ETH / -$21.11M one-day; -101,144 ETH / -$235.17M seven-day.
- `@TheMoneyApe` claims BlackRock ETFs sold $1.296B of ETH over 30 days with no day of net buying. This post has lower engagement than the major flow and on-chain posts, and the exact claim should be treated as unverified chatter; however, it is directionally consistent with the repeated ETF outflow data.
- Arthur Hayes de-risking appears across sources: `@CryptoHayes` says “I dumped it all,” and `@lookonchain` reports $22.28M sold including 6,400 ETH worth $15.2M, then another 14M ENA sold and $28.8M sold over 24 hours with most profits from ETH and ENA.
- Ethereum OG selling is a recurring theme: wallets inactive for years depositing ETH to Coinbase or selling, including 2,119 ETH to Coinbase, 1,500 ETH sold after 9 years of inactivity, another 1,500 ETH sold, and 7,594 ETH sold by an OG linked to the Ethereum Foundation.
- `@WhaleFactor` reports ETH losing multi-month uptrend support around $2,357, identifies $2,683 as the neutral-zone reclaim threshold, and sets a downside extension target near $1,800.

**Contrarian bullish evidence:**
- `@WatcherGuru` reports Tom Lee’s BitMine buying 10,452 ETH worth $24M, one of the higher-engagement bullish posts in the sample.
- `@lookonchain` reports a “smart trader” opening a $63.88M ETH long after the drop and later opening a 25x $45.34M long, though these are leveraged positions and not necessarily durable spot demand.
- A whale bought 4,000 ETH, deposited it into Aave, borrowed USDC/USDT, and moved funds to Binance to buy more ETH, suggesting leveraged accumulation.
- A whale with 93,184 ETH longs added $5.67M in margin to avoid liquidation, which reduces immediate downside liquidation risk but leaves the position vulnerable.
- A short seller was liquidated 13 times, illustrating how crowded or fragile bearish leverage can be near lows.

**X signal:** The event flow is bearish: price breaks, ETF outflows, liquidation cascades, prominent seller activity, and long-horizon OG selling. The bullish side is real but mostly tactical or contrarian: whale dip-buying, leveraged longs, corporate/fund purchases, and margin maintenance rather than broad demand recovery.

## Cross-source divergences and alignments

**Alignment:** StockTwits, X, and Reddit all align on the absence of bullish conviction. StockTwits is explicitly bearish; X is dominated by negative price, flow, and seller events; Reddit is mostly neutral but contains no bullish ETH-USD community narrative. The strongest cross-source bearish link is Arthur Hayes/Maelstrom: he appears in both X and Reddit as an institutional-style risk-off seller, reinforcing the negative flow narrative.

**Divergence:** The main divergence is between spot accumulation and ETF/OG selling. StockTwits includes a high-profile claim that 225,000 ETH was bought off exchanges in a single day, and X reports whales, BitMine, and leveraged traders buying the dip. Against that, ETF flows are repeatedly negative, and OG/Hayes selling is also negative. This suggests a market where supply is rotating toward aggressive traders or funds buying weakness, while established holders and ETF demand are not providing consistent support.

**Another divergence:** Reddit is much less bearish than StockTwits. r/ethereum had little direct market commentary, and r/CryptoCurrency was more abstract/ecosystem-focused. This means retail trading sentiment on StockTwits is more capitulatory than the broader Reddit narrative, which is mostly muted.

**News gap:** Yahoo Finance being unavailable removes a potentially moderating institutional source. Without it, the sentiment read leans more heavily on X and StockTwits, which are faster but less stable sources.

## Dominant narrative themes

1. **Risk-off macro overhang.** ETH-USD is being traded as a high-beta crypto asset in response to Fed policy, persistent inflation, rising oil prices, and geopolitical tension. The posts repeatedly connect ETH weakness to broader risk-asset pressure rather than to a single Ethereum-specific failure.

2. **ETF demand deterioration.** Repeated ETH ETF net outflows across Oct 27–29, plus the cited $485M outflow from Oct 14–22, are a central bearish signal. This suggests institutional/passive demand is not offsetting spot or OG supply.

3. **Prominent seller activity.** Arthur Hayes, Ethereum OGs, and long-dormant wallets are recurring negative catalysts. These supply narratives undermine confidence because they imply experienced or low-cost holders are reducing exposure.

4. **Technical breakdown and liquidation risk.** ETH falling below $2,350/$2,300, loss of multi-month support, liquidation clusters, and downside targets near $1,800–$2,000 create a momentum-driven bearish narrative.

5. **Contrarian accumulation is present but not dominant.** BitMine/Tom Lee buying, whale purchases, exchange net outflow claims, and leveraged longs show there is a bull case. However, most bullish X evidence is position-taking rather than confirmed durable demand, and StockTwits bullish labels remain sparse.

## Catalysts and risks surfaced by the data

**Bearish catalysts:**
- Continued ETH ETF outflows, especially if daily outflows reaccelerate above the Oct 28–29 trend.
- Additional OG or long-dormant wallet sales, which are highly visible on social feeds and create psychological overhang.
- Further macro risk-off moves tied to Fed policy, inflation data, oil, or geopolitics.
- A decisive break below technical support with lower liquidation targets near $1,900/$2,000/$1,800.
- Failure of leveraged whale longs to survive without adding margin, which could amplify downside.

**Bullish or stabilization catalysts:**
- Confirmation of sustained net exchange withdrawals or large one-day net buying, as claimed by StockTwits users.
- Continued accumulation by funds or high-visibility buyers such as BitMine/Tom Lee.
- Reclaim of $2,683 as a technical neutral-zone bridge, which could reset the breakdown narrative.
- ETF outflows slowing or reversing.
- A successful inverse head-and-shoulders or bottom pattern forming on higher timeframes, as referenced in StockTwits.

**Key risks to the sentiment read:**
- Yahoo Finance data is unavailable, removing an institutional news cross-check.
- StockTwits sample is small and concentrated within about 45 minutes on Oct 29, so it may reflect a single market pulse rather than the full week.
- Reddit sample is small and lacks engagement metrics, so community sentiment is hard to weigh.
- X provides high-quality event evidence, but some bullish posts describe leveraged positions rather than spot conviction.
- The BlackRock ETF-selling claim from `@TheMoneyApe` has lower engagement and is not independently confirmed by other posts, so it should be treated as directional sentiment rather than fact.

## Summary of key sentiment signals

|---|---|---|---|
| Retail tone capitulatory | Bearish | StockTwits | 7 user-labeled bearish posts vs 2 bullish; posts include “complete destroying,” “this goes to Zero,” “dead as fuck,” “bye bye.” |
| Retail bottom-fishing pocket | Mildly bullish | StockTwits | `@BullMine` bullish “bottom signal”; `@9owls` claims 225,000 ETH bought off exchanges in one day. |
| Price structure breaking down | Bearish | X / StockTwits | `@WhaleFactor` cites loss of multi-month support near $2,357 and $1,800 downside target; StockTwits users cite $1,900–$2,000. |
| ETF demand negative | Bearish | X | Repeated `@lookonchain` ETF flow updates show ETH ETF net outflows; `@coinbureau` cites $485M net outflows Oct 14–22. |
| Institutional/prominent holder de-risking | Bearish | X and Reddit | Arthur Hayes/Maelstrom sold ETH/ENA/UNI book; reported by `@lookonchain`, `@CryptoHayes`, and Reddit. |
| Long-horizon OG selling | Bearish | X | Multiple dormant ETH wallets sold or moved ETH to Coinbase, including Foundation-linked OG selling 7,594 ETH. |
| Macro risk-off pressure | Bearish | X | Fed hold, inflation, oil, geopolitical tension linked to liquidations and ETH falling below $2,300. |
| Whale/fund dip accumulation | Bullish | X and StockTwits | BitMine/Tom Lee bought 10,452 ETH; whales opened large longs and added to ETH positions. |
| Community narrative muted | Neutral to bearish | Reddit | No bullish Reddit posts among on-topic ETH sample; discussion mostly operational or fee-related. |
| Data-quality limitation | Neutral | News / Reddit / StockTwits | News unavailable; StockTwits clustered in one day; Reddit sample small and unranked. |

## Overall interpretation for the trader

ETH-USD sentiment during the observed window is **Bearish**, driven by retail capitulation, negative ETF flows, technical breakdown chatter, and visible selling by prominent holders and long-dormant wallets. The most credible counter-signal is aggressive dip buying from whales, funds, and leveraged traders, but this appears more tactical than structural and is not enough to offset the negative flow and narrative evidence.

The confidence level is **low** because Yahoo Finance news is unavailable, StockTwits messages are highly time-clustered, and Reddit provides only a small sample without engagement counts. The trade signal is therefore best treated as a bearish sentiment overlay that should be combined with verified on-chain exchange flows, ETF flow data, spot volume confirmation, and technical levels before any directional conclusion.

Anything between 2159.18 and 2406.51 is a fight zone, and in a fight zone the moderate position is smaller exposure, tighter invalidation, and no leverage.

The event calendar is the main reason I would not endorse the trader’s SELL as a standalone action. The October 31 hack-resolution market is priced at 60% odds, with recent large-exploit probability jumps indicating near-term security risk that is disproportionately negative for EVM-linked ETH-USD demand narratives. November 3 and November 4 bring midterms, and December brings the Fed. The prediction markets price a hawkish regime, which is structurally unfavorable to ETH-USD, but a Fed hold against 74% hike odds could trigger a violent relief rally. That asymmetry is exactly why new shorts should be small, conditional, and not placed into the current bar or a broad event window without explicit exits. I would also treat the visible whale longs as two-sided, not merely liquidation fuel. The $63.88M long, 25x $45.34M long, and 93,184 ETH whale margin add show that downside could be forced selling if 2159.18 breaks, but they also show that a defensive hold or macro relief could create short-covering pressure. A neutral risk view does not treat liquidity pools as one-way fuel.

The sentiment data supports caution in both directions. The bearish tone is real, with retail capitulation, ETF outflows, Arthur Hayes de-risking, and long-dormant Ethereum OG selling. But confidence is low because Yahoo Finance news is unavailable, StockTwits messages are highly clustered within one evening, Reddit is muted, and some bullish evidence involves leveraged positioning rather than durable spot demand. That weakens the aggressive certainty while also weakening the conservative idea that flat is automatically neutral. The best response is not “short ETH-USD because sentiment is bearish,” and it is not “ignore everything because sentiment is unreliable.” The best response is “keep ETH-USD flat or reduced, and only act when price, volume, momentum, and event outcomes align.”

So my challenge to the aggressive analyst is that the plan is too eager to monetize a medium-term downtrend inside a long-term structure that still has life, with poor location, inconsistent stops, and event-window blind spots. My challenge to the conservative analyst is that pure waiting can become too late, and that refusing to manage correlated portfolio risk is not the same as capital preservation. My moderate proposal is therefore not to execute the trader’s SELL at current price. I would hold ETH-USD neutral to underweight, with no new long, no market-dump short at 2262.34, and no fresh tactical short until either a confirmed rejection in the 2340-2407 area with a tight stop near 2407, or a confirmed breakdown below 2252.86 into 2159.18 with volume, RSI below 30, and widening MACD. Position size should remain very small, perhaps half of the trader’s proposed 4-5% notional, no leverage, and with any short exposure cut ahead of the October 31, November 3-4, and December FOMC windows. If the portfolio needs risk reduction, I would prefer reducing correlated gross exposure rather than creating a new ETH-USD directional position. In short, the sustainable middle path is conditional sell, not sell.
